reuse.why: Puts the rule into the existing getScheduledAmount and the API field calls it, but inlines the 7.5% tolerance instead of using getApproxNumberThreshold and leaves the forecast and budget-template midpoint copies untouched.

duplication.why: Three call sites keep their own missing/number/range dispatch and call the helper only for the range branch, and two other copies of the midpoint rule (forecast-schedules.ts, schedule-template.ts) remain alongside the helper.

placement.why: The rule itself lives in shared/schedules.ts where the tree keeps schedule amount logic; the problem is that callers still decide part of it.

scope.why: Only the amount rule, the API field and tests; no unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: The approximate branch in the helper is unreachable from the posting, action-sync and preview paths because they handle numbers before calling it, two paths still use the midpoint, and comments now claim 'furthest from zero' while the code uses the lowest value.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule and shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions return numeric amounts themselves before reaching getScheduledAmount; forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and budget/schedule-template.ts keep their own midpoint.

disguised_duplication.where: The leftover dispatches and midpoint copies are the pre-existing inline code left in place, not reshaped copies.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gained an op parameter (defaulting to 'isbetween') and an isapprox branch; three call sites wrap it in their own null/number dispatch that skips that branch, and forecast-schedules.ts and schedule-template.ts bypass it entirely.
